beats.care: Your college club or band could be part of it. Registration is open on bengalurujatre.in.
beats.what: GBA says 300+ organisations, including IIM-B and NGMA, and 80 artists like Swarathma have joined Bengaluru Jatre.
beats.why: The idea is a city-wide festival where neighbourhoods, colleges, companies and NGOs host their own events.

cards.body: Artists on the list include Swarathma, Aditya Prakash Ensemble, Manasi Prasad and Mystik Vibes. Resident associations have also enquired, and GBA expects more confirmations.
Events spread across the city instead of one big ground.
cards.caption: days, Dec 4–13

cards.body: "There is no single format," says minister Krishna Byre Gowda, so groups can shape their own events.

cards.q: Would your college host a Jatre event?

opts: It's spread across the city with no central venue
cards.q: What makes Bengaluru Jatre different from a usual festival?
cards.why: Instead of one ground, groups host events in their own neighbourhoods under the Jatre name.

hook: A festival with *no main venue*? Bengaluru is trying one in December

learn.t: Bengaluru Jatre has no central venue; events happen across the city under one shared name.

sources.name: Deccan Herald
sources.title: 300 organisations, 80 artists sign up for Bengaluru Jatre: GBA

tldr: Over 300 organisations and 80 artists have signed up for Bengaluru Jatre, a 10-day citywide festival from Dec 4 to 13.
watch: Festival runs December 4–13; colleges, RWAs and groups can register at bengalurujatre.in.
